column1: # What a long Treasury DID across the Nasdaq-like declines since 1962, on the model bond's footing:
# the record the Nasdaq set's `bond growth-crash` and `bond infl-crash` rows are graded against.  For
# every decline of 15% or worse in Ken French's HiTec industry portfolio from 1962-01-03 to 2026-06-30,
# the bond's LOG return over the same peak-to-trough span, in percent, and its empirical duration
# over that span.  Each episode is read as bondPct x 13.5 / duration, and the regime medians, by the
# model's own median (the upper-middle element), are +3.76 growth (16 episodes) and -3.33 inflation
# (6); `BondCrashSuite` / `bond_crash_tests` re-derive both from the rows below.  The S&P set's record
# is crash-response-1962-2026-10-05.tsv, the same reading over the market's declines.
# Sources, published: the equity is the HiTec column of Ken French's 10_Industry_Portfolios_Daily
# (value-weighted; computers, software, electronics), the public series the Nasdaq records are
# extended on; the bond and CPI are crash-response-1962-2026-10-05.tsv's (a 20-year par Treasury
# from FRED's DGS20, its 1987-1993 gap filled with DGS30's daily changes; FRED's CPIAUCSL).
# duration: minus the slope of the bond's weekly (5-session) log return on the weekly change of the
#   20-year yield over peak..trough; the par bond's modified duration at the peak's yield where the
#   span holds fewer than four weeks.
# cpiPeak / cpiTrough: CPI year over year at the peak and the trough, percent.
# regime: inflation when CPI year over year ROSE over the decline and stood at 4% or more at the
#   trough, else growth -- the rule the model reads on its own CPI.  Under it 2021-12-27..2022-11-03
#   is a growth episode (CPI 7.17 -> 7.12), as the 1980-82 disinflation is.
